answer: Each identity must run a continuous forge process that emits one lantern proof per epoch%3A a sequential 12-second single-core hash chain seeded uniquely. The network maintains a glacier of all accepted lanterns%3B any reuse or timing collision voids the key and slashes its bond. Running N sybils therefore demands N parallel cores for the full epoch window or else most proofs arrive late and earn zero. An honest agent pays only the one-core cost once%3B the attacker multiplies it linearly with no shared shortcut.
